title: Concurrency Safety Net Operationalization
summary: Operational kickoff to translate concurrency safety-net design into runbook, canary orchestration, and measurable SLO gates. Discussed eviction heuristics, prewarm strategies, canary traffic shaping, and automation for graceful degradations. Agreed on experiments and owners for next week.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-22 10:30 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan, Sana, Marco, Priya + rotating engineers
Links referenced: /docs/safety-net-design (internal), spreadsheet: tinyurl.com/rw-concurrency-canary (placeholder), runbook draft link shared in chat

[00:00] Jordan: ok thanks everyone for joining on short notice, we'll try to be efficient here. main goal is to get the safety net operationalized for the upcoming slate canary.
[00:18] Sana: yeah the PM asked for two things: one, a low-risk canary path that won't blow through quota, and two, an oncall-friendly runbook for staged degradation.
[00:30] Marco: quick context — the design doc assumes continuous batching and prefix caching, but we saw tail spikes during the last internal beta when concurrency hit 850 per pool. so we need smoothing and a corridor.
[00:45] Priya: and timeline: canary launch is slated for 2026-04-06, so we have two weeks to lock the automation and run one internal soak.
[00:58] Jordan: great, so let's walk through the operational steps. Sana, can you summarize the safety thresholds you suggested?
[01:05] Sana: sure; primary gates: 99th token latency < 450ms, error rate < 0.5% for generation endpoints, and tail worker queue length under 600ms of backpressure. secondary gate is sustained cost delta less than 1.5x baseline. if any primary gate trips, we want automatic traffic steering to lower-cost model variants and an immediate alert to P0 channel.
[01:30] Marco: to do that we need metric hooks — per-model route p99 token latency, queue depth, and per-token cost estimate. we have the telemetry but need the pipeline to compute rolling 5-minute deltas for canary slices.
[01:47] Jordan: right, and the canary policy should allow roll-forward at 10/30/60% with two-hour holds unless metrics are green.
[01:55] Marco: one nuance — the runtime kernel fallback sometimes increases latency but reduces memory. that could trigger a false positive on the p99 gate. maybe the gate should be p99 generation latency excluding kernel-fallback periods?
[02:13] Sana: hmm, tricky. transcription note: Marco said "kernel fallback" but the ops alert may mislabel it as "kernel fall-off" in some dashboards. we need consistent naming.
[02:22] Priya: can we mark events as "fallback-mode" in traces so the metric pipeline can filter them out?
[02:28] Marco: yes we can add a tag, but the export takes 24h to reindex historically. for canary we only need forward-looking tags.
[02:36] Jordan: fine, add the tag and the canary gating will exclude fallback-mode spans. next: token eviction. what heuristics are we recommending?
[02:45] Sana: current suggestion: LRU-ish but weighted by prefix hit-rate — evict low-hit KV entries first; also we should prioritize eviction on worker-level before cluster-wide throttles. practically: if worker cache pressure > 75%, evict until 60% using a weighted LRU. label it as "KV-evict-v1" in runbook.
[03:06] Marco: note — transcription sometimes shows "K-V cash" in exported text. ha, humans will know.
[03:10] Priya: for canary slices, we want a controlled prewarm window: send synthetic requests for 15 minutes at target concurrency to populate kv cache, then ramp real traffic. otherwise the first minutes look terrible.
[03:22] Jordan: synthetic prewarm is key. who's owning the synthetic traffic harness?
[03:27] Marco: infra can own the harness and Priya will own the orchestration playbook that calls the harness.
[03:33] Priya: yes, infra will run the harness in the test pool; release eng will flip slices in production once prewarm reports ok.
[03:40] Sana: also add a cooldown — if prewarm is insufficient, we shouldn't proceed; return to canary 0 and open ticket.
[03:47] Jordan: ok. let's talk automation for fallback: what do we want to automate vs manual?
[03:52] Marco: automated routing to compatible model variant on high error or high latency. manual for region-level reroutes. automation should be reversible with a single rollback command.
[04:03] Priya: build an endpoint in console to flip fallback policy per-slice, with audit log. Devops needs RBAC knob.
[04:10] Sana: security note: any automation that moves traffic to a different model variant needs to preserve data residency and encryption invariants — ensure KMS policies are identical.
[04:19] Jordan: good catch. Marco, add a KMS check to the route migration playbook.
[04:24] Marco: will do.
[04:26] [05:00] Speaker: (background) small cross talk about calendar conflicts, nothing critical.
[05:20] Jordan: let's map out the experiment plan for next week: one internal canary in us-west, synthetic prewarm, 6-hour soak at 30% traffic, then 2-hour ramp to 60% if green. metrics to observe: p99 token latency, generation error rate, worker queue depth, token cost delta, and KV hit ratio.
[05:40] Priya: and capture traces to evaluate if quantized kernels increase tail latency. we need the A/B traces labeled.
[05:50] Marco: remember quant profiles — if we flip quantization profiles we should test model quality too; evaluation harness needs to run prompt sets in parallel.
[05:58] Sana: quality regressions are a blocker. define acceptable regression as <0.8 points on the in-house BLEU-like metric or no significant hallucination increase.
[06:13] Jordan: sounds reasonable. next, alerting: what thresholds and paging rules?
[06:19] Sana: page at p99 > 600ms sustained over 3 consecutive five minute buckets or error rate > 1%. but for canary we want a noisy warning channel first — slack -> #canary-warnings and only page if it persists.
[06:33] Priya: we need a runbook link in slack alerts with clear next steps: scale up pool? flip slice? manual eviction? open bug.
[06:42] Marco: add a quick revert (traffic-0) API call in alerts that authorized people can hit to drop canary to 0% immediately.
[06:49] Jordan: make sure we have audit log and SSO gating for that button.
[06:55] [07:10] Sana: ops note — oncall will need a short cheat sheet: check kv hit ratio, check worker memory, check fallback-mode tag, then press revert if needed. keep it under 6 steps.
[07:25] Jordan: good. now handoff: who's patching the runbook? Priya?
[07:29] Priya: I'll author the runbook draft, Marco will add infra commands and synthetic harness links, Sana will write the paging thresholds and troubleshooting flow. Jordan will review.
[07:38] Jordan: deadline? can you all have a draft by EOD Friday?
[07:42] Priya: yes, EOD Friday (2026-03-26).
[07:45] Jordan: cool. action owner mapping then.
[07:48] [08:00] Marco: quick tech aside — caching eviction should be observable at worker-level metrics; let's add a worker_kv_evict_count metric to Prometheus, and an annotation when eviction runs.
[08:11] Sana: and emit a "prewarm-complete" event to event-bus with success/failure so orchestration can gate rollout.
[08:18] Marco: orchestration will use that event. we'll add a 10-minute timeout.
[08:23] Priya: synthetic harness will run at target concurrency for 15 minutes or until 90% KV hit ratio; harness returns pass/fail.
[08:33] Jordan: ok fine. let's walk through an incident scenario for the runbook test: assume p99 spikes during ramp to 60% and KV hit ratio drops below 40%. what are explicit steps?
[08:46] Sana: step 1: cut canary to 0 using the revert call, step 2: inspect eviction and worker logs, step 3: if eviction didn't free enough memory, manually trigger worker-level eviction, step 4: escalate to infra if disk pressure present.
[09:02] Marco: and capture heap profiles to see if kernel fallback thrash is causing repeated allocation.
[09:08] Priya: we should also schedule a postmortem cadence: 24h note, initial triage within 2 hours, postmortem artifact within 72 hours.
[09:19] Jordan: yes. make that in the runbook.
[09:24] [10:00] Speaker 2: (murmur) discuss potential competitor behaviours if their APIs degrade — irrelevant for internal ops but someone mentioned scaling heuristics from other vendor.
[10:12] Marco: we talked about prioritizing worker eviction over global throttles because global throttles cause mass-tail latency. micro-throttles are less visible externally.
[10:22] Sana: quick note on cost: if we route to a lower-cost variant frequently we may double token cost due to cold start overheads; monitor hour-by-hour cost and set an economic stop condition.
[10:34] Jordan: okay. any open technical blockers?
[10:37] Marco: infra needs an endpoint for instant revert with RBAC and audit. implementation is ~2d of work.
[10:44] Priya: orchestration needs the prewarm event integration — ~1d.
[10:48] Sana: metrics pipeline needs the fallback-mode filter — ~1d but depends on infra tagging roll out.
[10:55] Jordan: sounds like a three-day critical path; we'll prioritize and make sure release window is clear.
[11:02] [11:30] Jordan: let's capture concrete next steps and owners now.
[11:35] Priya: I'll write the runbook draft (owner: Priya) due 2026-03-26 EOD.
[11:42] Marco: infra will build revert endpoint and synthetic harness (owner: Marco) due 2026-03-24 EOD.
[11:52] Sana: metrics will add fallback-mode tags and worker_kv_evict_count (owner: Sana) due 2026-03-24 EOD.
[11:58] Jordan: I'll coordinate the internal canary and schedule the soak once we have the harness and runbook.
[12:04] Priya: one more thing — add a short FAQ section in the runbook for the oncall about what to check in console and who to call.
[12:12] Jordan: yep. ok any final comments?
[12:17] Marco: minor — can we include a quick test harness for quality evaluation that runs 100 prompts from the eval set during prewarm? small script, 1-2 hours run.
[12:26] Sana: yes add it as optional but recommended.
[12:30] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene Friday if necessary.

Recap (verbatim at end):
- Prewarm harness + synthetic traffic to populate KV cache before canary.
- Add fallback-mode trace tags and filter them from p99 gate.
- Implement instant revert endpoint with RBAC & audit.
- Run the internal canary in us-west: 30% 6-hour soak, then ramp to 60% if green.
- Run quality eval in parallel to monitor quantization regressions.

References shared in chat: runbook draft link, infra harness PR, spreadsheet with gating thresholds.

End of transcript.
